artifacts.summary: Empirically confirms the FTS5 AND-all-terms recall defect and the unsanitized '<'/'>' syntax-error gap in literature-briefing.sh --global, and recommends a per-term/grouped search-and-merge-by-rank fix plus sanitize_query() hardening.

memory_candidates.content: SQLite FTS5 MATCH treats bareword queries as an implicit AND of every term. A free-text query built from a full task description (15-30+ words) will essentially never match any document, since it requires ALL terms present in one row. When building a search feature from long free text, split into short per-term or small-grouped queries and merge results by BM25 rank instead of issuing one long AND-all query. Verified empirically with a live in-memory FTS5 table.

SQLite FTS5's query-string grammar treats '<' and '>' as syntax tokens outside of quoted phrases and throws 'fts5: syntax error near "<"' on a bare MATCH query containing them (confirmed live). Any FTS5 query sanitizer that already strips other syntax characters (':', '/', '(', ')', unquoted '*', bare AND/OR/NOT) should also strip or escape '<' and '>' -- easy to miss since they are not part of the commonly-cited FTS5 special-character list.

In this repo's literature extension, FTS5 phrase-quote-retry and trigram fallback rungs (literature-search.sh's do_search ladder) are syntax-error-safe but NOT a general recall improvement: wrapping a long multi-word string in one quoted phrase requires the exact word sequence (or trigram substring) to appear contiguously in a document, which is nearly as restrictive as the AND-all-terms primary rung for realistic long queries. Verified empirically: a 6-word phrase query against a document containing all 6 words as separate (non-contiguous) tokens returned zero rows.
